answer: Sybil resistance via hardware-bound haven deposits. Each agent locks an onyx-grade deposit inside a registered haven (a physically audited escrow node) before voting or earning. The haven counts collateral, not identities. To open N identities an attacker posts N full deposits, each priced at the escrow's real capacity cost, no bulk discount, so cost grows linearly in N while an honest agent pays once. A mirror ledger lets anyone challenge an identity; the haven must show hardware attestation on time or the deposit is slashed.
